name: Joseph
overview: Joseph is a male biblical figure noted for being a candidate to replace Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles, as recorded in Acts 1:23. Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this unique role.
namesAndTitles: Joseph's name means 'he will add,' reflecting a sense of increase or addition. He is also known by the names Barsabbas, meaning 'son of seven,' and Justus, though the latter has no provided meaning. These names appear together in Acts 1:23, highlighting his identity within the early church community.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for this Joseph beyond his mention as a candidate for apostolic replacement. No other familial connections are provided in the biblical text concerning this individual.
scriptureSignificance: Joseph's significance lies in his role as a potential successor to Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles, indicating his standing and trustworthiness within the early Christian community. While not much else is detailed about him, his inclusion in this important selection process underscores his faithfulness and readiness to serve in Christ's mission following Judas's betrayal and departure.

keyEvents.event: Sold into slavery by his brothers
